correctness.rationale: Central symmetry lets an inscribed disk be centered at zero, and projection of the coordinate normals to the plane makes the inradius (1-z^2)^(-1/2), z=min_i|U_i|. With a>=b>=z, strict a<b+z is exactly the hexagon criterion: all three pairs of cube faces then meet the plane in segments through their relative interiors. If a>b+z the largest-coordinate faces miss the plane and the other pairs give four edges. The tied generic boundary has zero Haar mass. On one sign/order chamber parametrize the other two components as sqrt(1-z^2)(cos t,sin t); the area element is dz dt and t ranges from theta(z) to pi/4. The six-edge subinterval begins at max(theta, pi/4-phi); the crossover a=2z,b=z is z=1/sqrt(6). The 48 sectors have normalization 12/pi times their angular lengths, giving both subdensities and no atoms. Direct differentiation gives the stated Jacobian in R. If z>1/sqrt(6), a>=b+z would force 1>=6 z^2, impossible, so the all-direction claim holds even for nongeneric normals. At (a,b,z)=(2,1,1)/sqrt(6) the largest-coordinate pair meets only at two opposite vertices and the other pairs supply four edges, giving the sharp bound. The conditional probability is strictly increasing below the cutoff, then constant one, not strictly increasing on the whole support. The claimed strict association still follows: for any nondecreasing g not essentially constant, a level separating values on positive-measure lower and upper sets permits pairs with the lower radius also below the cutoff. Both differences in the independent-copy covariance product are then strictly positive on a positive-measure set. The finite clipping/quadrature checker was inspected but not run or treated as a continuum proof.
residual_risks: Density-based conditional statements use the specified version; no claim is made for off-center sections, other dimensions, or non-Haar normals.
